spec.title: Brief: utility-scale solar costs
spec.request: Write a one-page brief on how utility-scale solar costs changed, citing at least 3 sources.

criteria.description: Cites at least 3 sources, and every cited link loads
Every direct quote appears word for word in the cited source

deliverable.name: brief.md
deliverable.content:
# Utility-scale solar costs

Costs kept falling. According to the 2025 review, "the levelized cost of electricity from new utility-scale solar fell by 12 percent between 2023 and 2025" (https://energy-observatory.example/reports/solar-2025).

Storage changes the economics: "in several markets, solar-plus-storage bids now undercut new gas peaking plants" [2].

The binding constraint has shifted to grid access, since interconnection queues are the main bottleneck (https://policy-review.example/2025/interconnection).

[2]: https://grid-journal.example/articles/storage-pairing

https://energy-observatory.example/repor.body:
Home · Research · Data · About · Subscribe

Solar Cost Review 2025

The levelized cost of electricity from new utility-scale solar fell by 12 percent between 2023 and 2025, driven mainly by cheaper modules and faster construction.

Module prices reached historic lows in late 2024 as manufacturing capacity grew faster than demand. Balance-of-system costs declined more slowly.

Methodology: figures are compiled from public filings, regulator datasets and interviews, and are revised when better data becomes available. Earlier editions of this analysis are archived and remain available on request.

spec.title: Brief: remote work and productivity
spec.request: Summarize recent evidence on remote work and productivity, citing at least 3 sources.

criteria.description: Cites at least 3 sources, and every cited link loads
Every direct quote appears word for word in the cited source

deliverable.name: brief.md
deliverable.content:
# Remote work and productivity

Hybrid arrangements look neutral for output and good for retention: workers "were as productive as office-based colleagues and were one third less likely to quit" [1].

Fully remote setups show weaker collaboration on complex projects (https://workplace-survey.example/2025-results).

Time savings partly flow back into work: "remote workers reallocated roughly 40 percent of the time saved from commuting to their primary job" (https://commute-study.example/time-savings).

[1]: https://labor-econ.example/papers/hybrid-trial

https://labor-econ.example/papers/hybrid.body:
Home · Research · Data · About · Subscribe

A randomized trial of hybrid work

In a six-month randomized trial, employees allowed to work from home two days a week were as productive as office-based colleagues and were one third less likely to quit.

Promotion rates did not differ between the groups.

Methodology: figures are compiled from public filings, regulator datasets and interviews, and are revised when better data becomes available. Earlier editions of this analysis are archived and remain available on request.
